description: Adds retries to an HTTP POST, reusing one request across attempts.

bugs.summary: The request and its bytes.Reader body are built once; the first attempt drains the body, so every retry sends an empty body (or fails on the Content-Length mismatch).

bugs.anchor: lastErr = fmt.Errorf("post %s: server error %s", path, resp.Status)
bugs.summary: A 5xx response is dropped without closing its body, leaking the connection on every retried attempt.

description: Moves a token bucket from float to integer counts.

bugs.summary: Elapsed time is truncated to whole seconds, yet last is reset on every call, so a bucket called more than once a second never refills.

description: Replaces a ledger-wide mutex with per-account locks.

bugs.summary: Locks are taken in argument order, so concurrent A->B and B->A transfers deadlock; a transfer to the same account locks one mutex twice.

description: Adds expiry to a read-through cache.

bugs.summary: item is redeclared with := inside the if, so on a miss Get returns nil and on expiry it returns the stale item instead of the fresh one.
TimeoutMs is milliseconds but is now multiplied by time.Second, making every timeout 1000 times too long.
Goroutines write the results map concurrently without a lock: a data race that can crash with a concurrent map write.

description: Parallelizes a user sync and adds a top-scores helper (TypeScript).

bugs.summary: forEach ignores the async callbacks' promises, so syncUsers records the sync and returns before any upsert finishes, with counts of zero.
sort() without a comparator orders numbers as strings (10 before 9), and it sorts the caller's array in place.

description: Adds in-place pruning and pagination of sessions (Python).

bugs.summary: Removing from the list while iterating it skips the element after each removal, so consecutive expired sessions survive.
Floor division drops the last partial page: 11 sessions at 10 per page report one page.

description: A correct retry loop for an idempotent PUT. Control case: any medium or high finding is a false positive.
